  - Tingling in right toes once after a run.
  - Training for marathon; increased running in past month.
  - Past ice hockey injury with large bruise to knee a few months ago.
  - History of far-sightedness, previously treated with LASIK surgery.
  - History of severe UTI, previously mistaken for possible kidney stones.

Management Plan

- Advise to continue ice therapy for knee injury.
- Recommendation to ease up on running, particularly if experiencing knee pain.
- NSAID/anti-inflammatory prescription (stronger than current ibuprofen) to be taken with food; not to be used concurrently with ibuprofen.
- Referral to physiotherapist for detailed assessment and examination of knee.
- Plan for further assessment or imaging if knee does not improve or after physiotherapy evaluation.
- Advised urgent re-presentation if the following occur: persistent swelling, heat, redness in knee, high temperature, feeling unwell, or knee locking/inability to bend or stretch.
- Prescription sent to pharmacy.
- Patient educated regarding when to seek urgent review.
